name: upper-midwest-herps
label: Upper Midwest (MN, WI, IA, ND, SD, MB, ON): reptiles and amphibians

groups.label: reptiles
groups.note: the GBIF backbone has no class Reptilia: turtles (Testudines) and snakes and lizards (Squamata) are classes of their own there

minRecordsNote: herps have far fewer open (CC0 / CC BY) records than birds (most iNaturalist observations are CC BY-NC): every species with 5 to 9 records in a region is a native of it (Western Ratsnake, Six-lined Racerunner, Smooth Softshell, Western Ribbon Snake, Sagebrush Lizard, Northern Dusky Salamander), while those under 5 are mostly escapes and misplaced records (Pig-nosed Turtle, Brown Anole, Cottonmouth)

merge.why: Ontario's ratsnake is the Gray Ratsnake (P. spiloides); most of its records sit on the older name P. alleghaniensis
two backbone keys for Desmognathus fuscus (one DOUBTFUL); one salamander

drop.why: 'Amblystoma spec': salamanders identified to genus only, a doubtful backbone name, not a species
'Ambystoma unisexual': the unisexual (hybrid-origin) salamander complex, not a species and not told apart from Blue-spotted or Jefferson Salamander in a photo
Testudo nebrascensis is a fossil tortoise of the Badlands; the records are fossils catalogued with a recent year

Anaxyrus fowleri.why: Wikidata's label is the old scientific name ('Bufo Fowleri')

Pituophis catenifer.why: the subspecies of this region (P. c. sayi) and the name used here; Wikidata names the Pacific subspecies

Nerodia sipedon.why: the name used in this region's field guides (Northern Watersnake); Wikidata has 'Common Watersnake'

Pantherophis spiloides.why: the name used in Ontario (see merge)

Terrapene carolina.why: the name used in North America

Trachemys scripta.why: the form found here (released pets); Wikidata names the species 'Pond Slider'

Ambystoma texanum.why: the spelling of North American field guides

Desmognathus fuscus.why: the name used in Ontario; 'Dusky Salamander' alone is ambiguous beside the Allegheny Mountain Dusky Salamander
